             # Set to yes to start on boot. If setting this remotely, be sure to add a rule
             # to allow your remote connection before starting ufw. Eg: 'ufw allow 22/tcp'
            -ENABLED=no
            +ENABLED=yes
             
             # Please use the 'ufw' command to set the loglevel. Eg: 'ufw logging medium'.
             # See 'man ufw' for details.
   run      ufw --force enable
            # turn UFW on: load the rules and the default deny together
   note     Turns UFW on with default deny incoming. The allow rules (allow in 22/tcp from anywhere; allow in 2222/tcp from anywhere; allow in on tailscale0; allow in 22/tcp from anywhere (v6); allow in 2222/tcp from anywhere (v6); allow in on tailscale0 (v6)) are written to UFW's rules files before the policy loads, and load with it in one step.
   note     Closes to the internet (the default deny drops new connections to them): tcp/5432 (postgres). Allow one with `ufw allow` before applying if it must stay public.
   note     Published container ports are not affected: Docker forwards them past UFW's input rules (DKR-001). The ufw-docker step filters them.
   note     Containers that connect to a service on the host itself (host.docker.internal, the bridge gateway) go through UFW's input rules too, and close unless a rule allows them.
   note     Connections that are already open, this SSH session among them, stay up: UFW accepts established traffic.
   note     UFW's forward policy, ip_forward, Docker's firewall settings and /etc/ufw/sysctl.conf are left as they are.
   undo     Restore the UFW files the step changed from the backup and turn UFW off again (ufw disable), as it was before.
            ufw disable
